text.p: Broker Day Cutten Ltd has issued a hold recommendation for Adelaide Bank Ltd, saying a slowdown in earnings growth is expected in 1996/97 as growth in lending volumes and margins ease.
However analyst Nick Ross said the price to book value ratio remained a relatively modest 1.6 multiple.

Prospective 1998 price earnings ratio of 10.3 times was at a seven percent premium to the estimated bank average with the dividend yield at a slight discount, he said in the broker's annual South Australian Companies Review, published this week.

Ross said his forecast 1996/97 net operating profit after abnormals had been scaled back by A$1 million to A$27 million, a 3.8 percent rise on 1995/96, to reflect a slowdown in lending volume growth, tighter margins and a rise in the tax rate.
Adelaide Bank reported a 24 percent rise in profit after tax to A$26.02 million in 1995/96.
"Net profit growth in 1996/97 is expected to fall to 3.8 percent. Margins will clearly be under pressure in the coming year," Ross said in the report.

Growth in lending volumes would be sourced predominantly from outside South Australia in the coming year, with more cross selling of products interstate, that is selling both a mortgage and insurance to customers, he said.
Adelaide Bank shares closed at A$4.51 on Wednesday compared with A$4.05 at the time the report was written.
